events.title: Proposed ruling: escalate (model confidence 0.90)
events.body:
This file is filed as a safety dispute: the rider's complaint states the driver "kept making comments about my body and asked for my number" and that she "felt harassed and unsafe" — on its face an unwanted-sexual-advances / harassment allegation, which is the category SAFE-1 sends to a human reader rather than to automatic adjudication. Both advocates reach the same procedural conclusion (C1, C3, D1), and the execution trace confirms the only permitted outcome is escalation, so no ruling on the merits is issued.

The record on the disputed words is thin both ways. There are no in-app chat messages at all [F3], and the only written statement is the driver's post-trip denial, "I made small talk. Nothing inappropriate happened." [F4] — a unilateral statement written after the trip. The rider's account therefore rests on her complaint alone, and the driver's denial cannot be verified against any system record either: absence of a chat record neither convicts nor exonerates, which is precisely why SAFE-1 requires a human reading of the original record rather than a finding here.

None of the system records bears on the allegation. GPS shows the ride essentially on the optimal route: 17.1 km actual vs 17.2 km optimal, -0.1 km (-0%) [F1], duration 25.8 min vs 23.6 min estimated, +2.2 min [F2]. These facts settle route and time only; they are neutral as to speech, so they neither corroborate nor contradict the rider's narrative, and no fare, toll, stop or no-show fact exists in this file.

The fare is unaffected on this record. The trip is a fixed-quote RydeX service, charged $35.70, and the actual distance (17.1 km) is below the optimal route (17.2 km) [F1], so there is no unexempted deviation and no meter-based top-up to compute under RD-2/RD-1; the complaint before me is about conduct, not the fare, and no monetary award is made.

Profile facts are context only and decide nothing. Rider: 129 days on the platform, rating 4.5, 0 disputes in 90 d, 0 upheld [F5]. Driver: 327 days, rating 4.67, 999 trips in 90 days, 0 disputes, 0 upheld in 90 d [F6]. Neither record can establish or refute the allegation, and F6's clean history is not a basis for the main finding — it is offered only against account action (D4, C5), and I apply no account action here.

For the reviewer: what happened — alleged body comments and a request for the rider's number during a 25.8-minute RydeX trip between 22:29 and 22:54 [F1][F2]; what is disputed — whether any such remarks were made, denied in [F4]; which facts to check — the original complaint narrative, the absence of in-app messages [F3], the driver's post-trip statement [F4], and both parties' account records [F5][F6]. Because the allegation is harassment-type conduct and the written record cannot settle it, this goes to a person under SAFE-1.

ruling.recommended_action: Refer to RydeHELP human reviewer: rider alleges harassment (body comments and a request for her number) during RydeX trip Woodlands Civic Centre → Punggol Waterway Point, pickup 22:29, drop-off 22:54; interview both parties on the original record, and advise the rider of the RydeHELP reporting path (and 995 if she needs medical assistance). No fare adjustment: fixed RydeX fare of $35.70 is unaffected because the actual distance (17.1 km) was under the optimal route (17.2 km) [F1]. Do not apply any account action on this record alone.

claims.assertion: The rider's complaint states that the driver 'kept making comments about my body and asked for my number' and that she 'felt harassed and unsafe' — this is a harassment / unwanted-sexual-advances allegation of exactly the kind SAFE-1 covers, and it must be read by a human on the original record rather than auto-decided.

The chat record contains no in-app messages at all (F3) and the driver's own written statement, made only after the trip, says 'I made small talk. Nothing inappropriate happened.' (F4) — the conduct the rider complains of was therefore never exchanged in writing; the only contemporaneous source is the rider's complaint, so the driver's post-hoc denial cannot be verified against any system record either.

A harassment screen is mandatory in every case and does not depend on a keyword hit or on chat evidence (F3, F4); because the allegation is 'unwanted sexual advances'-type conduct of the sort Ryde's Code of Conduct says 'will not be tolerated' and results in 'immediate termination and legal action where applicable', the correct output here is escalate to a person, not a fare ruling.

Nothing in the system records contradicts the rider's account: GPS shows the ride ran essentially on the optimal route (17.1 km actual vs 17.2 km optimal, F1) in 25.8 min vs 23.6 min estimated (F2), so no fare or route fact exists that could be used to explain away or discount what happened in the car during those 25.8 minutes.

The rider has 0 disputes in 90 days and 0 upheld (F5) while the driver has 999 trips in 90 days with a 4.67 rating and 0 disputes, 0 upheld (F6); these profiles are context for the human reviewer only and are not offered as proof that the harassment occurred — profile facts cannot decide this case.

weaknesses: The chat record is empty (F3) and the driver's statement (F4) denies wrongdoing: there is no verbatim written message from the driver containing the body comments or the request for the rider's number, so the harassment rests on the rider's complaint alone and the judge cannot verify the words from any record.

The driver's statement (F4) is a direct denial ('Nothing inappropriate happened'), and the driver's profile (F6: 999 trips in 90 d, 0 disputes, 0 upheld) is the kind of clean-history fact the driver will use to argue the allegation is out of character.
The rider's own profile (F5) shows a 4.5 rating and no prior disputes, which gives the other side no lever, but it equally proves nothing about this trip.

The GPS facts (F1, F2) show an essentially optimal route and normal duration, so there is no independent system record — no detour, no stop, no anomaly — corroborating that anything unusual occurred during the ride.

No fare, toll or no-show fact exists for this dispute type, so I cannot ask for any monetary adjustment even if the rider also wants the trip refunded; the only relief available on this record is escalation to a human, with any refund or account action left to Ryde's discretion.

claims.assertion: The complaint alleges body comments and a request for the rider's number — on its face a harassment / unwanted-advances allegation, which is exactly the category SAFE-1 reserves for human review rather than automated adjudication; I do not concede it occurred, but the correct procedural route is escalation, not a ruling against my client.

The only record of what was said is F4, the driver's written statement 'I made small talk. Nothing inappropriate happened.'; there is no in-app message (F3: no chat messages between rider and driver), so the record contains no message, quote or timestamp of any specific remark by which the contested words could be found.

The rider's own history gives no corroboration: F5 records 0 disputes in 90 days and 0 upheld against any counterparty, so there is no pattern of prior similar complaints by this account that would weight the narrative either way.

My client's account record is clean and long: F6 shows 0.9 years on the platform, a 4.67 rating, 999 trips in 90 days, and 0 disputes and 0 upheld in 90 days (route: 0, no-show: 0); under the profile evidence this supports the account being a long-standing, non-abusive one and weighs against any flag_account action.

Nothing in the trip data shows unsafe or abnormal driving: F1 records actual 17.1 km against an optimal 17.2 km (-0.1 km, -0%) and F2 records 25.8 min against 23.6 min estimated (+2.2 min), i.e. the direct route, so there is no route-deviation or dangerous-conduct component to add to the complaint.

weaknesses: The rider's complaint at intake (the statement being adjudicated, referenced alongside the file) squarely alleges harassment-type conduct — body comments and a request for the rider's number — which on its words engages SAFE-1 and SAFE-2 and is the kind of allegation the policy removes from automated decision-making; the judge will read that narrative directly.

F4 is the driver's own written statement and is contradicted by the rider's complaint; and while chat facts lose to gps/timeline/fare facts when they conflict, the harassment allegation is not covered by any gps, timeline or fare record here (F1, F2 are neutral on speech), so no system record rebuts it — the case therefore turns on two unverifiable accounts.

F6 shows the driver's rating is 4.67, not perfect, and profile facts may never decide the main finding, so it cannot carry the case; F5 likewise cuts only weakly for the driver, since a rider with 0 prior disputes has no history of false complaints.

My client chose to make 'small talk' late at night (pickup 22:29) with a solo rider; F4 concedes conversation occurred, so the driver's own account does not exclude the possibility that talk crossed a line, and nothing in the file records what was actually said.

points.response: Agreed on the procedural route: an unwanted-advances allegation goes to a person, not to an automated ruling — that is precisely the escalate I already asked for in C3, so the driver gains nothing by conceding the route; what matters now is that the human reviewer receives the rider's account, not that the driver 'does not concede' it.

Accepted that no in-app message exists (F3) and that F4 is the driver's own post-trip wording; but the absence of a chat record means the contested words were never captured, so F3/F4 cannot exonerate the driver any more than they can convict him — and a driver's unilateral statement is not evidence of what he did not say, which is exactly why SAFE-1 sends this to a reader rather than closing it.

This cuts the rider's way as much as the driver's: F5's 0 disputes in 90 days and 0 upheld means there is no history of unfounded complaints from this account, and a first-time report is not weakened by being the first — profile facts are only context and cannot decide the finding anyway.

F6 (0.9 y, 4.67 rating, 999 trips, 0 upheld) is exactly the use of profile facts the policy forbids as a basis for the main finding, and 4.67 is not a perfect record; I ask for no flag_account against the driver in this brief, so the point is aimed at an action I did not request.

F1 (17.1 km vs 17.2 km optimal) and F2 (25.8 min vs 23.6 min) show an ordinary route and duration, which I already accepted in C4 — but 25.8 minutes in a closed car at 22:29 is where the alleged conduct occurred, and no GPS, timeline or fare fact in this file records or refutes speech, so SAFE-1 is still engaged.

Conceded as to procedure only: the rider's narrative engages SAFE-1, and escalation to a human is the correct channel, not a ruling against my client. My D1 already accepts escalation for that reason; escalation is a transfer of the question, not a finding that harassment occurred.

The rider is right that no system record rebuts the spoken allegation, but the gap runs both ways: F3 shows zero in-app messages, so there is no recorded wording, timestamped message or contemporaneous note supporting the rider's version either. F4 remains the only account of the conversation, and it denies wrongdoing.

The mandatory SAFE-1 screen requires escalation, which I do not resist, but the Code of Conduct consequence the rider quotes ('immediate termination and legal action where applicable') attaches to a violation, and no clause permits treating an unproven allegation as established - the rider concedes there is no supporting record (their C2, C5).

F1 (actual 17.1 km vs optimal 17.2 km, -0.1 km) and F2 (25.8 min vs 23.6 min estimated, +2.2 min) show an entirely ordinary ride, so the system records neither corroborate nor contradict the narrative; the rider cannot convert the absence of a contradicting record into affirmative evidence.

Agreed that profile facts cannot decide this case: F5 and F6 are context only, and F6 (0.9 years, 999 trips in 90 d, 0 disputes, 0 upheld) is offered by me solely to oppose any flag_account or adverse account action against my client, not as proof the allegation is false.
